meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'follow'.

examples.text: Ты будешь со мной таскаться каждый день?
examples.trans: Are you going to follow me around every day?

examples.text: Это слово «таскаться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'follow' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
goes right before the word it negates
polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

ездить.gloss: to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive

meanings.en: to go by vehicle (habitually or round trip), to drive, to ride

examples.text: И в сауну я не езжу.
examples.trans: And I don't go to saunas.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'купать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'buy up'.

examples.text: Вы будете скупать алкоголь во всех магазинах.
examples.trans: You'll buy booze at every store.

examples.text: Это слово «скупать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'buy up' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'alcohol' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you planning to drink alcohol?

examples.text: А если он откажется от алкоголя?
examples.trans: And what if he refuses alcohol?

examples.text: Вы хотите добавить алкоголь в еду?
examples.trans: Do you want to add alcohol to food?

meanings.note: пойти в магазин = to go to the shop

examples.trans: What to do? Let's go to the shop.

meanings.note: в долгу не остаться = to repay a favour

examples.text: Помогите мне! Я в долгу не останусь.
examples.trans: Help me! I'll pay you back, I promise.

examples.text: Я хотел уберечь тебя от ошибок.
examples.trans: I wanted to protect you from mistakes.

examples.text: Мой долг уберечь вас от этого.
examples.trans: It's my duty to protect you from this.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: adds a reason or an obvious truth

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'жраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'get hammered'.

examples.text: Лева, я ведь все равно нажерусь.
Это слово «нажраться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'get hammered' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Just to spite you and your boss.

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: всё получилось = it all worked out

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'висимость'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common substantive noun meaning 'addiction' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я спасу вас от этой зависимости.
examples.trans: I will save you from this addiction.

examples.text: Это слово «зависимость» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'addiction' is often heard in conversation.
